newsitem.title: USA: Costly U.S. foreign crudes garner tepid interest.
newsitem.headline: Costly U.S. foreign crudes garner tepid interest.

text.p: U.S. refiners showed tepid interest in foreign crudes Thursday with most continuing to focus their attention on less costly domestic grades and shorter-haul barrels from Latin America.

The trans-Atlantic arbitrage remained closed, with the spread between January West Texas Intermediate/Cushing and Brent narrowing to 70-75 cents, down 10 cents from late Wednesday. The spread was 90-95 cents for the corresponding February month, down 15 cents from Wednesday.
A European company sold 500,000 barrels of Brent to a U.S. Gulf Coast refiner for arrival at the end of December at a delivered price Jan WTI plus 10 cents.
Traders speculated that the crude was brought out of Caribbean storage, because the notional price for bringing barrels across the Atlantic is around WTI plus 40 cents.
The closed arb window has pumped up demand for Louisiana Light Sweet, which traded as high as WTI plus $1.10 a barrel earlier in the week before settling back to plus 72-80 cents Thursday afternoon.
"LLS is still the best deal in town. The next best deals are Cusiana and Cano Limon," one trader said.
From Latin America, a U.S. Gulf Coast refiner picked up a cargo of Cano Limon for an undisclosed price.

Meanwhile, Chile's state oil company Empresa Nacional del Petroleo (ENAP) bought one million barrels of Escravos from Chevron for Dated Brent plus 25 cents a barrel fob, and two 400,000 barrel cargoes of Oriente from Tripetrol for Jan WTI minus $4.25 a barrel fob for early January, market sources said.

Separately, Colombia's state oil company Ecopetrol late last week sold 400,000 barrels of South Blend for Jan WTI minus $2.35 a barrel fob, traders said. The cargo was heard to have gone to a refiner in Central America.
In the U.S. aftermarket, a bevy of deals were transacted. Paper Brent spreads for December/January changed hands at 56 cts and 59 cts.
A series of partial outright Brent trades fell between $23.15-20 a barrel. A full boat traded at $23.23 a barrel, 10 cts over the IPE close.
